title: Blue Penny Museum
about_landmark_text: Step inside this museum on the Caudan Waterfront, dedicated to the history and art of Mauritius since it opened in November 2001, and you're standing feet away from two of the rarest stamps on Earth. Its centrepiece is a pair of 1847 "Post Office" stamps - the one-penny orange-red and two-pence blue - designed off the back of Britain's Penny Black and stamped with Queen Victoria's profile.
interesting_fact: A consortium of Mauritian companies, led by the Mauritius Commercial Bank, paid $2,000,000 in 1993 just to bring the stamps home after almost 150 years abroad. To protect them from light damage, the real stamps are only illuminated for ten minutes on the quarter-past of every opening hour - the rest of the time, what you're looking at is a facsimile.

title: Port Louis Casino
clue_text: head southeast for about half a km - you are looking for a ship
puzzle_question: How many claws at the front of the boat?
puzzle_explanation: The casino's facade is built to resemble the bow of a pirate ship, complete with a bowsprit mast and figurehead-style statuary - the claws are part of that theatrical, ship-themed design.
about_landmark_text: This casino at Caudan Waterfront is part of the complex that opened on 25 November 1996, on land once occupied by warehouses and a meteorological observatory. It occupies the Barkly Wharf building, named for Sir Henry Barkly, Governor of Mauritius from 1863 to 1870, and is known for a striking facade styled like the bow of a pirate ship, complete with bowsprit mast and statuary.
interesting_fact: The building's pirate-ship facade - a bowsprit mast and figurehead-style statues built into the architecture - makes it one of the more theatrical pieces of commercial design on the whole waterfront, and it backs it up with scale: it's the largest casino in Port Louis, running 214 gaming machines and 16 table games under that pirate-ship roof.

title: SAJ Statue
clue_text: head along the waterfront - you are looking for a statue
puzzle_question: The taller of the 2 PM statues, how tall is it in metres?
puzzle_explanation: At 3.6 metres, the SAJ statue stands about 30cm taller than the neighbouring Ramgoolam statue - a height difference that drew its own share of public comment when it was unveiled in 2024.
about_landmark_text: This bronze statue of Sir Anerood Jugnauth ("SAJ") was unveiled at the Port Louis Waterfront on 15 June 2024, honouring the former Prime Minister and President who dominated Mauritian politics for decades. It stands beside an earlier statue of Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam, placing two of independent Mauritius's most prominent leaders side by side on the same esplanade.
interesting_fact: At 3.6 metres tall, the SAJ statue was built about 30 centimetres taller than the neighbouring Ramgoolam statue, and its Rs 13.5 million cost and sculptor Devanand Bungshee's likeness both drew public criticism at the time of unveiling.

title: Aapravasi Ghat World Heritage Site
clue_text: keep going in the same direction for about 350m - you are looking for a museum
puzzle_question: To the nearest 10% - what percentage of current Mauritians descend from the people this museum celebrates?
puzzle_explanation: Roughly 70% of Mauritians today are descended from the indentured labourers who passed through this depot between 1849 and 1923 - making it one of the most significant sites anywhere for understanding the roots of modern Mauritian society.
about_landmark_text: You're standing at the place where the modern indentured-labour diaspora began - though the practice itself predates this exact building. The first 36 indentured labourers reached Mauritius on 2 November 1834 aboard the ship Atlas, which had left India that September; they landed near the old Customs House, just metres from where you're standing now, fifteen years before this purpose-built depot even existed. Built in 1849, the Aapravasi Ghat - literally the 'Immigration Depot' - became the main entry point for almost 500,000 indentured labourers brought to Mauritius between 1849 and 1923, mostly from India but also China, Africa, Madagascar and Southeast Asia, to work the island's sugar plantations after the abolition of slavery. New arrivals bathed after weeks at sea, were medically inspected and vaccinated against smallpox, had their contracts read aloud in their own language, and usually spent about two days here completing the paperwork before being sent out to sugar estates across the island. It's been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2006.
interesting_fact: Roughly 70% of Mauritians today are descended from these indentured labourers - making this small 1,640 m² depot one of the most significant sites anywhere for understanding the roots of modern Mauritian society, and one of the earliest examples of a labour-migration system that would go on to reshape economies worldwide.

title: China Town South Gate
clue_text: next a short walk of about 170m in an Easterly direction - you are looking for a gate
puzzle_question: Which city gifted the gate to Port Louis?
puzzle_explanation: This is one of Chinatown's ornamental Friendship Gates, a gift from Foshan in Guangdong province - Port Louis's twin city in China.
about_landmark_text: This is one of the ornamental Friendship Gates marking the entrance to Port Louis's Chinatown on Royal Road, one of the oldest Chinatowns in Africa. The gates were a gift from Foshan, in Guangdong province, Port Louis's twin city in China, symbolising the long-standing links between the two places and the wider friendship between Mauritius and China.
interesting_fact: Chinatown's roots reach back to the 1780s, when the first Chinese migrants arrived in Port Louis from Guangzhou aboard British, French and Danish ships - making it one of the oldest continuously inhabited Chinese communities anywhere in Africa.

title: Manga Street Murals
address: Venpin Street, near Emmanuel Anquetil Street, Chinatown, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: keep heading down Queen St then take a quick right and a left - you are looking for something artistic
puzzle_question: What country does this style of art originate?
puzzle_explanation: The anime and manga-style artwork lining Venpin Street channels Japanese pop culture, painted almost single-handedly by local artist Urmila Narsiah in 2020 to mark 50 years of diplomatic ties between Mauritius and China.
about_landmark_text: Bright anime eyes, mid-strike swordsmen and mist-wreathed heroines cover the shopfront shutters and walls along this narrow stretch of Venpin Street, near its corner with Emmanuel Anquetil Street - a lane Chinatown locals nicknamed "Manga Street" the moment the paint went up. Before 2020 it was just another derelict back alley behind Chinatown's main strip. The New Chinatown Foundation handed the walls over to volunteer artists that year to mark the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Mauritius and China, and in a matter of weeks a forgotten passage became one of the most photographed corners of Port Louis.
interesting_fact: Mauritius's borders were shut for Covid when these murals went up in 2020, so there was no flying in an international street-art crew - the entire wall of Japanese manga and anime characters was painted almost single-handedly by one local artist, Urmila Narsiah.

title: Jummah Masjid
address: Royal Road, Queen St, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: now you are heading inland - cross the road carefully and prepare for it to get noisy - turn left at Queen St - walk another block and start looking for a religious building
puzzle_question: How many vintage lamp posts outside the Queen St Entrance?
puzzle_explanation: Royal Road's Queen Street entrance to Port Louis's principal mosque is flanked by a pair of vintage lamp posts, part of the late-Victorian rebuild finished in 1895.
about_landmark_text: Step onto Royal Road in the heart of the old commercial quarter and Port Louis's principal mosque rises in front of you, known simply as Jummah Masjid. The city's mercantile community bought this plot on Queen Street in 1852 and consecrated the mosque a year later, when it went by a different name entirely - the "Mosque of the Arabs." What you're looking at today is largely a late-Victorian rebuild: a major expansion begun in 1878 under Jackaria Jan Mahomed dragged on for years, slowed by disease and building-supply shortages, and wasn't finished until 1895.
interesting_fact: The mosque blends Indian, Creole and Islamic architectural styles so seamlessly that it's often named one of the most beautiful religious buildings in Mauritius.

title: Central Market Port Louis
clue_text: next head west south west as the crow flies about 300m, but it is about 450 to walk - you are looking for a market
puzzle_question: What object sits above the main gate to the market?
puzzle_explanation: The market's wrought-iron main gate, dating from 1839, is topped with a clock - a small Victorian-era flourish on one of the city's best-loved pieces of period ironwork.
about_landmark_text: Step into the historic heart of Port Louis's daily life - a market that's been trading here, in one form or another, since 1828, moving to this site in 1833 and formally opening under British rule in 1839. Its wrought-iron gates, worked with floral motifs and dating from that same year, are one of the city's best-loved pieces of Victorian-era heritage; the building itself was heavily renovated between 2001 and 2004 after several fires, careful to keep its original character intact.
interesting_fact: For nearly two centuries this market has been where all of Mauritius's communities meet and trade side by side - Creole, Franco-Mauritian, Indian, Chinese and African - and locals still often call it the Bazaar or Victoria Market rather than by its official name. A serious fire tore through the market in 1996, badly damaging the building - the renovation that followed, running 2001 to 2004, was as much about repairing that fire damage as modernising a market that was already over 150 years old.

title: Statue of William Newton
clue_text: head to Place d'Armes - you are looking for a statue, but which one? This one shares a name with a famous scientist
puzzle_question: His descent is Mauritian and which other country?
puzzle_explanation: Sir William Newton was born in 1842 to an Indo-Mauritian mother and a Scottish father - a mixed heritage that placed him inside the very racial divide he spent his career fighting to close.
about_landmark_text: This statue honours Sir William Newton (1842-1915), a Mauritian lawyer of mixed Indo-Mauritian and Scottish descent who led the reformist movement launched in 1882 demanding an elected element in the colonial Legislative Council. His campaigning under the administration of Governor Sir John Pope Hennessy helped bring about the Constitutional Reform of 1885, which for the first time let Indo-Mauritians and other non-white islanders elect their own representatives.
interesting_fact: The Constitution Newton helped win came into force on 20 October 1885 - the first time in Mauritian history that non-white islanders could vote for their own representatives in the colonial legislature. Newton himself embodied the divide he fought to close: born in 1842 to an Indo-Mauritian mother and a Scottish father, he belonged to the island's "Gens de couleur" community that colonial law treated as second-class. He won a British scholarship to study law in England, came home to practise as a barrister, and led the Reform Party he founded for thirty years, right up until his death in 1915.

title: Port Louis Theatre
address: Remy Ollier St & Jules Koenig St, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: next you are looking for a theatrical venue - walk southeast about a quarter of a km
puzzle_question: In what year was its first stone laid?
puzzle_explanation: Governor Robert Farquhar laid the theatre's first stone in 1820; the doors finally opened two years later, on 11 June 1822.
about_landmark_text: This is the oldest theatre in the Indian Ocean region, and it's been putting on a show since 1822. Governor Robert Farquhar laid its first stone in 1820, architect Pierre Poujade built it in the style of a classic London playhouse, and the doors opened on 11 June 1822. Inside, three tiers of seating for around 600 people sit beneath an ornately painted dome of cherubs and chandeliers - for over a century, this was the island's only home for opera, drama and balls, until the Plaza Theatre opened in Rose Hill in 1933.
interesting_fact: The theatre has closed its doors more than once over the centuries - shut for two years in the 1890s by a cyclone and a run of epidemics, then for seven years during the Second World War - but nothing compares to its most recent closure: it shut in 2008 for renovation and didn't reopen until 2025, seventeen years later.

title: Statue de Saint Louis
address: St. Louis Cathedral's Garden, Pope Hennessy St, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: head down Jules Koenig St for about 300m - you are looking for another statue
puzzle_question: What is the king's regnal number?
puzzle_explanation: This is Louis IX of France - "Saint Louis" - the only French king ever canonised. His regnal number is IX, not to be confused with the much later Louis XVI.
about_landmark_text: A bronze statue of Saint Louis - King Louis IX of France, the cathedral and city's namesake saint - stands on a stepped stone pedestal in the peaceful courtyard and garden directly outside Saint Louis Cathedral, on Pope Hennessy and Bourbon Streets. It shares the square with a separate 18th-century heritage obelisk that once served as a water fountain, together forming a quiet corner right at the cathedral's front doors.
interesting_fact: Louis IX is the only French king ever canonised a saint - he led two Crusades and died of dysentery outside Tunis in 1270. Mauritius's oldest cathedral, and the streets around this square, all carry his name because of that dedication.

title: Photographic Museum Of Mauritius
address: Rue du Vieux Conseil, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: the next one is not so easy to find, it is a museum, down a backstreet, with a NEGATIVE cryptic link?
puzzle_question: What was the first name of its founder?
puzzle_explanation: The museum was founded in 1966 by photographer Tristan Bréville and his wife, to preserve Mauritius's photographic record going back to 1839.
about_landmark_text: This museum of historic photography sits on Rue du Vieux Conseil, founded in 1966 by photographer Tristan Bréville and his wife to preserve the island's photographic memory going back to 1839. Housed in an 18th-century building that once belonged to French botanist and administrator Pierre Poivre, it holds over 50,000 old photographs of Mauritius, alongside a collection of historic cameras and equipment.
interesting_fact: Among its collection is one of the rarest lenses in photographic history, made by Charles Chevalier for Jacques Daguerre - inventor of the daguerreotype - in 1834, just a few years before photography itself was publicly unveiled.

title: Natural History Museum
clue_text: head for a museum where you can find a real dodo (or part of one) and other wonders of the scientific world
puzzle_question: How many arches on its front façade?
puzzle_explanation: The museum occupies the ground floor of a National Heritage building completed in 1884, modelled partly on Sri Lanka's Colombo Museum - its arched colonial facade is one of the most photographed in Port Louis.
about_landmark_text: This is the Mauritius Institute's Natural History Museum, on the ground floor of a National Heritage building constructed between 1880 and 1884 and modelled partly on Sri Lanka's Colombo Museum. Its collections trace back to 1826, when naturalists Julien Desjardins and Louis Bouton first proposed a museum to the governor - the resulting Desjardins Museum opened in 1842, decades before the current building existed, and the institution was declared a National Museum in 2000.
interesting_fact: The museum's most complete dodo skeleton wasn't unearthed until 1904, discovered by a Port Louis barber named Étienne Thirioux, whose amateur fossil-hunting turned up two near-complete dodo skeletons - the finer one stayed here in Mauritius, the other ended up in a museum in Durban, South Africa. Remarkably, his discoveries went almost unrecognised by scientists for decades and were never properly described in scientific literature until long after his death.

title: Bust of Queen Victoria
address: Victoria Urban Terminal, Victoria Square, Port Louis, Mauritius
clue_text: next head to the Port Louis transport urban terminal - you are looking for a lady you might have seen earlier on the walk
puzzle_question: How many stones are visible on the necklace?
puzzle_explanation: Look closely at the necklace carved around her throat, sitting just above the medallion pinned to her sash - count the individual stones worked into it and you'll land on twelve, part of the same fine detail that had commuters assuming this bust must have been shipped in rather than carved locally.
about_landmark_text: Wrapped in cloth for its first two days on public view, this stone bust of Queen Victoria stands inside the Victoria Urban Terminal - the striking multimodal transport hub built over Port Louis's old Victoria Square bus station. It appeared here without warning in May 2023, as the terminal's redevelopment neared completion, carved with enough detail in the queen's crown and flower-worked robe that commuters passing through assumed it had to have been shipped in from abroad rather than carved locally.
interesting_fact: No plaque or inscription has ever said who carved it or why - and when it vanished under cloth just 48 hours after first appearing, word around the terminal was that officials were saving the reveal for 6 May 2023: the day King Charles III was crowned in London.

title: Caudan Arts Centre
clue_text: last stop - you are heading for another theatre, which forms part of a centre - cross the tram line over a bridge to find it
puzzle_question: What shape is the main feature of the large outside mural?
puzzle_explanation: The Caudan Arts Centre opened in December 2018, the first new theatre built in Mauritius in nearly a century - completing this walk back at the Caudan Waterfront, where it all began.
about_landmark_text: This performing-arts venue at Caudan Waterfront was built on what was once a car park, inaugurated in December 2018 as the first new theatre built in Mauritius in nearly a century. Its 431-seat auditorium, designed by architect Maurice Giraud and Didier Ho Architecture with acoustics engineering by Arup, hosts drama, music and dance, alongside a restaurant, bars, a conference room and exhibition space.
interesting_fact: Before this venue opened in 2018, Mauritius had gone almost 100 years without a purpose-built theatre - making the Caudan Arts Centre the first new stage of its kind on the island in nearly a century.
